hero_prop_criteria.center_of_focus: The story, a shot or a character's attention centres on the object.
hero_prop_criteria.high_frequency: The object is present in more than one scene/act.
hero_prop_criteria.transfer: The object passes between two characters.

scenes.heading: EXT. SABA ELIOR’S COURTYARD — LATE MORNING

hero_props.name: honey-date cakes
hero_props.description: A small set of three honey-date cakes Miri receives from Ima and guards, then later shares with Tav. They remain the same physical cakes throughout, though one is split and the set decreases from three to two to shared portions.
hero_props.reason: These cakes are the emotional engine of the opening and closing village scenes, repeatedly referenced across the story as the parallel to Yonah’s lunch; the entire lesson about generosity turns on whether Miri keeps or gives them away. They are also transferred from Ima to Miri and then from Miri to Tav, with repeated handling and discussion in multiple scenes.

appearances.heading: EXT. MIRI’S VILLAGE — MORNING
appearances.usage: Introduced as Miri’s prized snack; she counts and hides them, and Ima asks her to give one away.
appearances.evidence: “Three small HONEY-DATE CAKES gleam in the cloth.”

appearances.heading: EXT. VILLAGE LANE — MOMENTS LATER
appearances.usage: Miri carries them hidden in the basket while Tav notices and asks for one.

appearances.heading: EXT. SABA ELIOR’S COURTYARD — LATE MORNING
appearances.usage: Miri explains she has the cakes and worries about giving one to Tav; Saba discusses “fewer cakes.”

appearances.heading: EXT. HILLSIDE RIDGE — SUNSET
appearances.usage: Miri reflects that she should have given Tav the cake, connecting her lesson to the lunch miracle.
appearances.evidence: “I think I should have given Tav the cake.”

appearances.heading: INT. SCROLL ROOM — LATE AFTERNOON
appearances.usage: Back in the Scroll Room, the cakes are shown again as the unchanged remaining set in Miri’s bundle.

appearances.heading: EXT. VILLAGE LANE — SUNSET
appearances.usage: Miri finally gives Tav one whole cake and half another, then shares the remainder with Nim.

appearances.heading: EXT. SABA’S COURTYARD — EVENING
appearances.usage: Nim jokes about future generosity, and the cakes’ lesson lingers though the prop itself is no longer present on-screen.

hero_props.name: linen basket
hero_props.description: A basket of folded linen that Miri carries for Saba; it also becomes the vessel that holds or frames the hidden cakes and later the scroll-room basket imagery. The same basket is reused across the village and scroll-room scenes.
hero_props.reason: It appears in multiple scenes and is actively handled, first given to Miri by Ima, then carried to Saba, then used as the resting place for the cakes and later for Nim. It functions as a recurring physical container tied to Miri’s burden and her lesson about carrying and sharing.

appearances.heading: EXT. MIRI’S VILLAGE — MORNING
appearances.usage: Ima gives Miri the basket of folded linen.

appearances.heading: EXT. VILLAGE LANE — MOMENTS LATER
appearances.usage: Miri walks with the basket while hiding the cakes inside it.

appearances.heading: EXT. SABA ELIOR’S COURTYARD — LATE MORNING
appearances.usage: Miri brings the basket to Saba, who takes the linen from it.

appearances.heading: INT. SCROLL ROOM — LATE AFTERNOON
appearances.usage: The basket is back with Miri in the Scroll Room; she opens it to reveal the cakes.
appearances.evidence: “Miri looks down at the cloth bundle in her basket.”

appearances.heading: EXT. VILLAGE LANE — SUNSET
appearances.usage: Miri sits with the basket beside Tav while sharing the cakes; Nim’s own participation is framed by the basket nearby.
appearances.evidence: “Miri sits beside him and opens the cloth.”

appearances.heading: EXT. SABA’S COURTYARD — EVENING
appearances.usage: Nim climbs into the basket in the final scene, closing the object’s arc as a recurring home for the hidden goods.
